images.title: A right angle near the end
images.purpose: Show the right angle construction at a point O close to one end of a slanting line, with one compass setting making OX = OY.
images.composition: One slanting line from lower left to upper right; O near its lower left end; the new reddish purple line rising from O, with white space all around.
exact_structure: One long dark straight line from the lower left to the upper right of the frame at about 20° to the horizontal, ending a short way past O at the lower left.
A point O on the line, close to its lower left end, labelled O.
A small grey (#6B7280) arc centred at O cutting the line at X (towards the lower left end) and at Y (towards the upper right), labelled X and Y; OX and OY each carry one tick mark.
On the upper side of the line, a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at X and a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at Y, of the same larger radius, crossing at A, labelled A.
A reddish purple (#CC79A7) line from O through A, perpendicular to the slanting line, with a small square right angle mark at O.
One label 90° beside the right angle mark.
rejection: X drawn beyond the end of the line, or OX and OY of visibly different lengths
the line OA not perpendicular to the slanting line
images.takeaway: Even near the end of a line, a small equal radius from O gives X and Y, and one pair of equal arcs gives the right angle.
images.description: A slanting line with O near its lower end, a small arc giving X and Y, two equal arcs crossing at A and a reddish purple line OA at 90°.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Notice the small first radius that keeps X on the line, then check the SSS reason: OX = OY, AX = AY, AO common.

image_decisions.why: A tilted line with O near one end shows the method works in any position, unlike the centred example.
